etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French précaution, Latin praecautio, from praecavere, praecautum (“to guard against beforehand”); prae (“before”) + cavere (“be on one's guard”). See pre-, and caution.

definitions.definition: Previous caution or care; caution previously employed to prevent misfortune or to secure good

quote.citation: July 2, 1826, John Henry Newman, The Philosophical Temper, First Enjoined by the Gospel
quote.text: The ancient philosophers treasured up their supposed discoveries with miserable precaution.

definitions.definition: A measure taken beforehand to ward off evil or secure good or success; a precautionary act.
